graph_checkpoint_days.effect: Retain terminal graph checkpoints for at least this many days after their last save

schedule.effect: Run the daily scheduled sweep. false also skips admission collection; completion cleanup and landing cleanup still run

idle_days.effect: Minimum idle age before a lane cache or declared output is collected

free_floor.allowed: whole B, K, M, G, T or KiB to TiB; a plain number means GiB
free_floor.default: 1% of the state volume, capped at 5 GiB
free_floor.effect: Advisory free-space floor for admission, new builds and pressure collection; below it GC removes further eligible caches oldest first

lane_cargo_cache_max.effect: Cap all marked lane Cargo caches; evict oldest eligible caches first while retaining live, foreign and unobserved custody

alert_below.effect: Free space below which an applied collection emits one gc.low_disk note per dip

projects.{project}.regenerable.allowed: directory names; not .git, .worktrees, absolute or parent paths
projects.{project}.regenerable.effect: Git-ignored directory names collected at any depth in the project's linked worktrees; `.provenant/scratch` is collected in addition without a declaration

projects.{project}.keep.effect: Paths, their descendants and any matching directory containing them that collection preserves

projects.{project}.foreign_worktrees.effect: merged-clean removes clean, merged linked worktrees with no known writer after a complete free census

provider_state_days.effect: Days a terminal attempt's provider state stays resumable; reread on each sweep

logs_days.effect: Days before captures over 64 KiB and intermediate event rows of closed runs expire; the last 64 KiB is kept as a .tail file

session_revisions.effect: Checkpoint revisions a session keeps, the current one included; reread on each save

chair_log_days.effect: Days a chair log payload is kept

chair_log_entries.effect: Chair log entries kept per session

chair_log_bytes.effect: Chair log payload bytes kept per session

chair_log_replay_days.effect: Days chair log replay receipts are kept

projects.{project}.checkpoint_soft_bytes.effect: Advisory checkpoint size above which a save warns; the hard limit is unchanged

max_parallel.effect: Accounts per quota probe batch; batches and probes currently run sequentially. Out-of-range values refuse the file

wall_budget_seconds.effect: Wall-clock budget for a whole quota tick. Out-of-range values refuse the file

min_monthly_allowance_usd.effect: Lowest documented monthly allowance an OpenCode Go model needs to be routed or selected; a model with an unknown allowance is refused while the floor is on

update.effect: Run the detected native updater in a detached one-shot worker scheduled by quota events. Provider preparation briefly shares the update lock; running lanes do not hold it. If all candidates are updating, dispatch waits at most --wait (capped at 30 seconds), then uses the installed version. false opts out; {command: [program, argument, ...]} overrides the updater directly without a shell.

update_timeout_seconds.effect: Maximum native updater duration in the detached worker. Timeout kills the updater process group and records failure. Updater descendants retain the exclusive lease until exit, including descendants that leave the group.

update_interval_seconds.effect: Minimum time between update attempts, checked on existing housekeeping events. Failed and interrupted attempts and result-write errors wait the same interval.

runtime_deadline_seconds.effect: Cap on the wall-clock runtime of any lane on this provider. A dispatch's own --provider-timeout applies when it is shorter. At the deadline the provider is stopped and the attempt settles as timed_out, whatever the host did meanwhile, including sleeping.

profile_limit_bytes.effect: Maximum rendered macOS sandbox profile size. Increase for lanes with many grants; profiles pass through argv and may still hit OS limits.

writer_token_budget.effect: Default fresh-token budget for writer attempts. 0 turns the budget off. Run and template settings may override it; project and host settings supply lower layers, and the winning source is recorded with the limit.

projects.{project}.writer_token_budget.effect: Replace the host writer token budget for this project.

writer_budget_action.effect: Default response when a writer passes its token budget. A project's setting replaces the host setting; omitted settings use the compiled wrap_up default.

writer_budget_grace.effect: Fraction of the writer token budget allowed as grace before applying the budget action. A project's setting replaces the host setting; omitted settings use the compiled 0.1 default.

projects.{project}.writer_budget_action.effect: Replace the host writer budget action for this project.

projects.{project}.writer_budget_grace.effect: Replace the host writer budget grace for this project.

writer_budget_tiers.{tier}.token_budget.effect: Override the host writer token budget for this routing tier; omitted values inherit lower layers.

writer_budget_tiers.{tier}.on_budget.effect: Override the writer budget action for this routing tier; omitted values inherit lower layers.

writer_budget_tiers.{tier}.budget_grace.effect: Override the writer budget grace for this routing tier; omitted values inherit lower layers.

grant_limit.effect: Maximum total plan roots and entries in each provider profile family; authentication and native-control families retain minimum caps of 16 and 64. Increase for lanes needing more roots.

write_grant_limit_bytes.effect: Maximum encoded bytes of applied write grants recorded for a lane. Increase when an otherwise valid grant ledger exceeds the default; terminal records retain bounded headroom.

argv_prompt_limit_bytes.effect: Maximum prompt bytes passed directly to argv adapters. Larger top-level prompts spill to an attempt-owned file; nested attempts refuse rather than use a parent-writable spill. The overall 1 MiB prompt bound and operating-system argument limits still apply.

continuation_copy_limit_bytes.effect: Maximum retained provider state bytes copied into a continuation. Available disk space may lower the effective copy budget. Refusals report the setting and source; raise it or reduce state before retrying.

continuation_copy_entries.effect: Maximum entries searched or copied from retained provider state for a continuation. Refusals report the setting and source; raise it or reduce state before retrying.

continuation_copy_depth.effect: Maximum directory depth searched or copied from retained provider state for a continuation. Raising it does not relax credential, hard-link, filesystem or worktree-overlap guards.

source_view_seconds.effect: Total time allowed to build the pinned source view of a `review` lane. The view is built with one batched object read, so a healthy large repository needs far less. Raise it on a slow disk or a heavily loaded host.

source_view_entries.effect: Maximum files in a pinned source view. A larger tree is refused, naming this limit.

source_view_bytes.effect: Maximum total file bytes in a pinned source view. A larger tree is refused, naming this limit.

writer_writes.allowed: up to 16 absolute, safe directory paths outside credential roots
writer_writes.effect: Directories writer lanes may read, write and execute as subtrees; read-only lanes are unchanged

review_exempt.effect: Paths that do not count toward an uncommitted outcome; a project list replaces the host list and an empty list disables exemptions

sandboxed_routes.allowed: up to 64 route prefixes (adapter/model), printable ASCII
sandboxed_routes.effect: Routes whose lanes run sandboxed under default configuration, matched by prefix on the route id. Default is empty; users can add routes (e.g. OpenCode Zen tier opencode/opencode/). lanes.sandbox=off overrides listed routes with a warning; an empty list leaves the knob to decide.

sandbox_cache_reads.allowed: up to 16 absolute, safe directory paths outside credential roots
sandbox_cache_reads.effect: Host cache directories, such as a compiler cache, that a sandboxed lane may read but never write. Paths that do not exist at launch are skipped; a writer's own write root inside one keeps its write grant. Unsandboxed lanes are not limited by this list.

projects.{project}.sandbox_cache_reads.allowed: up to 16 absolute, safe directory paths outside credential roots
projects.{project}.sandbox_cache_reads.effect: Replace the host sandbox_cache_reads for this project; an empty list grants none.

push_conflict_markers.effect: Refuse pushes that add lines starting with <<<<<<< or >>>>>>>

projects.{project}.writer_writes.allowed: up to 16 absolute, safe directory paths outside credential roots
projects.{project}.writer_writes.effect: Replace the host writer_writes list for this project; an empty list grants no host-configured writer roots. Origin: host configuration [domains.run.projects.<project ID>].

poll_seconds.effect: Initial delay between pending land CI samples; later delays double up to four times this value. A per-command --poll overrides it.

batch_size.effect: Maximum pull requests in a batch.

approval.effect: What approves a pull request for batch landing: an independent forge review of its head, or an accepted Provenant delivery receipt whose review covers the head, carried over a merge-in or an unchanged rebase. Forge rules still apply at merge.

approval_tier.effect: What approval a pull request needs. none: CI only. carry: a review that still covers the head, a change after it that touches only tests, docs or review-exempt paths, or a review of the delta since. delta: as carry, but every change after the review needs its own review. auto is none for a pull request that touches only tests, docs or review-exempt paths, and carry otherwise.

publish_settle_seconds.effect: Time to wait before observing an unresolved publication again.

publish_unknown_warn_seconds.effect: Warn when a publication remains unknown for this long.

gate.executor.effect: Executor for the candidate command plan.

gate.pool.effect: Pool for candidate gate pricing; check issuer is the fallback.

gate.env_passthrough.effect: Credentials explicitly passed to candidate commands.

pr_ci.mode.effect: Pull request evidence policy; forge requirements still apply.

pr_ci.label.effect: Opt-in label for pull request CI.

post_merge.timeout_seconds.effect: Maximum time to follow post-merge checks.

budget.rate_micros_per_minute.{pool}.effect: Pool price in millionths of the configured currency per minute.

budget.advisory_micros.effect: Advisory amount in millionths of the configured currency.

budget.cap_micros.effect: Spending cap in millionths of the configured currency.

ci_poll_backoff.initial_seconds.effect: Initial delay after a pending CI observation. Each later observation doubles the delay up to max_seconds; the remaining CI timeout takes precedence. Zero makes the gate eligible at the next tick.

ci_poll_backoff.max_seconds.effect: Maximum per-gate polling delay. The 60-second scheduler interval determines the earliest automatic re-check.

ci_poll_overrides.<node_id>.effect: Override the host CI polling policy for one node ID. Values and origins appear in config show.

allowed_read_roots.default: empty (read roots stay inside the project and its registered worktrees)
allowed_read_roots.effect: Absolute host directories that template `read_roots` may name besides the project's own registered worktrees.

limits.expansion_depth.effect: Longest dependency chain in edges, root nodes at depth 0, and deepest composite nesting a graph may expand to. Graph documents cannot raise it.

limits.concurrency.effect: Graph concurrency limit. Zero uses host lane caps.

bundled.effect: Start from the bundled per-model policy (cache prices, compaction windows, lane guidance, result checks). false starts empty.

defaults.cache.read_share_target.effect: Advisory cache-read share a lane should reach; reported in stats, never enforced.

defaults.cache.price_multiplier.effect: Current price multiplier; divides the read-heavy preference weight.

defaults.cache.read_ratio.effect: Cache-read price divided by uncached input price.

defaults.cache.write_ratio.effect: Cache-write price divided by uncached input price.

defaults.cache.output_ratio.effect: Output price divided by uncached input price, for compaction break-even guidance.

defaults.cache.context_window.effect: Context window size; read-heavy preference needs at least 1000000.

defaults.cache.read_heavy_weight.effect: Weight multiplier for read-heavy and review work on cheap-cache models.

defaults.compaction.window.effect: Context size at which compaction is advised.

defaults.compaction.min_turns.effect: Fewest turns before compaction is advised.

defaults.lane.max_context.effect: Enforced largest context for a lane on this model.

defaults.lane.max_turns.effect: Enforced most turns for a lane on this model.

defaults.lane.stop_early_ok.effect: false asks writers to report completion through the shared handoff.

defaults.lane.user_skills.effect: Override host and project user skill discovery for matching routes. rules.policy.lane.user_skills uses the same values.

defaults.lane.read_only.effect: true refuses write lanes on this model.

defaults.result.check.effect: Check the result for the required sections before accepting it.

defaults.result.sections.allowed: exact section heading lines; empty clears
defaults.result.sections.effect: Heading lines a result must contain.

defaults.result.fallback.effect: Model for the one fallback attempt when the result check fails.

rules.allowed: tables with adapter, model, account, schedule {starts, expires as RFC 3339 timestamps, windows [{weekdays?, start_hour, end_hour}] in UTC} and policy (the same fields as defaults, under rules.policy); weekdays use Monday-based indexes, Monday 0 through Sunday 6
rules.effect: Layered overrides ordered by scope: global, adapter, model, account, model plus account; later rules win at equal scope. Schedule start is inclusive, expiry and window end are exclusive; an overnight window wraps midnight; inactive rules have no effect.

history_max_bytes.effect: Disk cap for each account's quota history under quota/history/. Readings go to a current file that rotates to one predecessor at half the cap, so the pair never exceeds it and the newest reading is always kept.

directories.effect: Optional list of absolute config directories, in addition to directory, that are signed into the same account, for example ~/.claude-anese and ~/.claude. At most 8. Schema only: nothing reads it yet; native session ingest will use it to attribute sessions to the account.

plans.form: array of tables, any number of entries

fields.name: Plan label, for example max_5x. At most 64 characters.
fields.price: Price per month in currency; 0 or more, 0 for a free plan.
fields.currency: Three capital letters (ISO 4217). USD when omitted. No conversion is applied.
fields.notional_usd: Optional list-price value in USD of a free or discounted plan, for example 20 for a student plan priced 0.
fields.effective_from: First day the price applies, YYYY-MM-DD (UTC).

plans.effect: Prices over time for the account. The entry with the latest effective_from on or before a reading applies to it, and quota history --json shows it as plan_price, with price and notional_usd. Dates must differ within an account; unknown keys, negative or non-finite prices and bad dates refuse the config. This is not the detected plan label, which comes from the provider or the account's plan option.

user_skills.effect: Discover host user skills for lanes read-only. off disables host user skill discovery unless overridden by domains.lanes.projects.{project_id}.user_skills or route policy lane.user_skills. Route policy wins over project, then host. Inspect value, default and origin with config show or config schema.

skill_stage_max_bytes.effect: Maximum bytes copied into an attempt's read-only user skill tree. Content exceeding the bound is skipped with a warning. Inspect value and origin with config show.

projects.{project}.capabilities.effect: Capabilities granted by default to this project's writer lanes; node settings and invocation flags may override them. Read-only lanes do not inherit them.

projects.{project}.shared_paths.effect: Existing paths shared read-write with this project's writers. Absolute, ~/ and primary-checkout-relative paths are accepted. Git, credential, protected and executable paths are omitted with a warning. Read-only lanes receive no additional writes.

projects.{project}.exec_roots.allowed: directory paths relative to the primary checkout
projects.{project}.exec_roots.effect: Read-and-execute directory subtrees relative to the primary checkout. Entries escaping that checkout, missing, protected, credential or writable targets are ignored with a warning naming the configuration key.

admission_policy.{rule}.effect: Override memory_pressure, process_budget, lane_cap, disk_floor or startup_spacing policy. Non-boundary queue warns and proceeds; refuse opts into immediate strict refusal. The effective key and source appear in diagnostics.

start_spacing_ms.effect: Advisory spacing window between starts of the same class. Its policy defaults to warn and never queues a launch.

memory_pressure_threshold.effect: Kernel memory pressure threshold for the memory_pressure policy rule. The rule defaults to warn; never disables its observation.

max_concurrent_builds.default: max(1, min(cores / cargo_build_jobs, GiB of RAM / 6))
max_concurrent_builds.effect: A build throttle, not a hard cap: cargo builds, tests, checks and lints that a lane's cargo shim runs at once across the host and every project that shares the state directory. Slots are advisory: a compiling command tries once, then warns and proceeds when busy. Cargo owns its build-lock queue. Direct ~/.cargo/bin/cargo, rustc and non-cargo builds are not gated.

lane_port_base.effect: First port of the range split into per-writer-lane blocks. A writer with an allocated block holds it for its lifetime and sees PROVENANT_LANE_PORT_BASE and PROVENANT_LANE_PORT_COUNT. Unreadable lane-port settings or allocation I/O errors warn and skip allocation.

lane_port_block.effect: Ports in each writer lane's block (PROVENANT_LANE_PORT_COUNT).

lane_port_blocks.effect: Blocks in the range, so the most writer lanes that hold a block at once; the base plus blocks times block size must be at most 65536. 0 turns allocation off. A writer launched while every block is held is not started and reports no free port block.

max_lanes.effect: Most lanes of any class live at once across the host; a lane beyond it queues and is refused with the limit and source.

max_project_lanes.effect: Most lanes of any class live at once for one project; at most max_lanes.

max_writer_lanes.effect: Most writer lanes live at once across the host; a writer beyond it queues and is then refused with a reason naming the cap.

max_project_writer_lanes.effect: Most writer lanes live at once for one project; at most max_writer_lanes.

cargo_build_jobs.default: Half the available cores, at least 1
cargo_build_jobs.effect: Default CARGO_BUILD_JOBS for lanes; an inherited value takes precedence.

cargo_incremental.effect: CARGO_INCREMENTAL for lanes. Incremental sessions grow a lane's target without bound and are rarely reused; a value already in the lane environment takes precedence.

cargo_debug.allowed: none, line-directives-only, line-tables-only, limited, full, 0, 1, 2, true or false
cargo_debug.effect: CARGO_PROFILE_DEV_DEBUG for lanes. Line tables keep backtraces at a fraction of the size of full debug information; a value already in the lane environment takes precedence.

build_dir_max_bytes.effect: Cap on the allocated bytes of all Cargo profile directories in lane caches, idle and busy alike. Collection removes idle directories, least recently used first, during manual or scheduled GC, when admission finds the disk below gc.free_floor, and in `provenant gc`; a directory whose Cargo locks are held is never removed. When busy directories alone exceed the cap, every eligible idle directory is removed and the total stays over.

build_dir_grace_seconds.effect: A profile directory whose newest file or directory modification is within this many seconds is never removed, even when its Cargo locks are free: test and run binaries execute after Cargo drops its locks, and Cargo may be opening its lock files. Zero removes the protection. It protects only recently written directories: a test or run binary that runs longer than the grace without writing under target/ is unprotected unless a Cargo lock is still held.

build_dir_survey_interval_seconds.effect: Minimum interval between lane-cache admission surveys. A breached free-space floor triggers a survey immediately; a previous survey near the byte cap also keeps surveys due on each admission. 0 surveys on every admission.

diversity.effect: How a review panel that cannot meet its `minimum_family_counts` is handled. advisory resolves the panel and records one warning per short family, with the required and met counts and the exclusions, in the review-family resolution and each reviewer's preamble; strict refuses the review instead. A run document's `[review]` table can set `diversity` for one review. A lens's own `required_family` always refuses when unmet.

\"<glob>\".add.default: bundled test-path rules (`**/tests/**`, `**/*.test.*`, `**/conftest.py` and others) add `tests`
\"<glob>\".add.effect: Add these review lenses, outside the slot cap and once, when a changed path matches the glob. The reason is recorded as `by_paths:<glob>` in `--explain` and the review report. Setting any `by_paths` table replaces the bundled rules; an empty `[domains.routing.review.lenses.by_paths]` removes them.

store_busy_timeout_ms.effect: Milliseconds a command waits for a contended local store, both the SQLite busy timeout and the stores' own advisory locks, before it reports contention. Read once when a command starts; zero fails fast

confinement.census_exclude_ancestors.effect: Exclude the invoking process's ancestor chain from live-writer detection at run admission. When false, only the invoking process itself is excluded, so an ancestor shell with its working directory inside the worktree is treated as a live writer.

confinement.census_ignore_unreadable.effect: Host-owned exact executable path and signing team_id (or platform) exceptions for actual cwd EPERM. All real/effective/saved uids must be system accounts foreign to every root owner; platform entries also require a root-owned chain with no group/other write permission. Listed executables may occupy a worktree. Invalid/unreadable signing state never qualifies. Not accepted through dispatch --knob or Fabric overrides.

routing.allow_unknown_partial_headroom.effect: Remove the ranking penalty for uncalibrated partial quota headroom below the limit.
routing.allow_unknown_partial_headroom.trade_off: Unknown coverage warns and stays eligible by default. Accepting it removes the preference penalty; measured exhausted lower bounds still refuse.

routing.workload.effect: Describe the task for model policy. Read-heavy and review work give cheap-cache, million-token models a configurable preference in pools.
routing.workload.trade_off: A preference preserves model choice and readiness gates; it does not force every read-heavy task onto one model.

routing.exclude.effect: Keep each listed provider (claude), account (label, entry or adapter/key) or exact model (adapter/id) out of named-route pools for every task. A standing list; `--exclude` and a graph's list are added to it, not substituted for it. A pinned `--model` is never affected.
routing.exclude.trade_off: Selection still weighs pacing and readiness over the remaining members, but an exclusion that empties a pool refuses the dispatch rather than widening it.

routing.flag_exclude.effect: The exclusion list one dispatch carries, set by advanced route resolution. Same selectors as `routing.exclude`; refusals and `--explain` name the flag as the source.
routing.flag_exclude.trade_off: Applies to this dispatch only; the standing `routing.exclude` list and a graph's list still apply.

routing.graph_exclude.effect: The exclusion list a graph passes to each node it launches, set from graph routing policy. Same selectors as `routing.exclude`; refusals and `--explain` name the graph as the source.
routing.graph_exclude.trade_off: Applies to every node's named-route pool; a node's pinned model is never affected.

routing.depletion_wait_seconds.effect: Longest quota reset, in seconds, a depleted writer waits for instead of handing its work to another agent. 0 never waits: a usage-limited, model-unavailable or login-expired stop moves to the next eligible route at once (same model on another account, another provider or family at the same tier, an adjacent tier, a host-native sub-agent), and reaches the chair only when none is eligible. The order and the tier adjacency are `domains.routing.depletion`.
routing.depletion_wait_seconds.trade_off: A wait keeps one account's session and cache but idles the node until the reset; the hand-off starts a fresh attempt on another route immediately. A reset beyond the bound never waits.

usage.project_attribution.effect: Include the existing project identifier in local usage events.
usage.project_attribution.trade_off: Off keeps project identity out of usage logs; on makes project-level usage visible to anyone who can read them.

fabric.accept_handoff.effect: Let a Fabric peer start a Claude session on this host through a session hand-off.
fabric.accept_handoff.trade_off: Off refuses every hand-off with HANDOFF_DISABLED; on lets a peer open an unconfined session under a registered account.

config.history_max_entries.effect: Keep at most this many entries in the configuration history; the oldest are dropped first.
config.history_max_entries.trade_off: A higher count keeps a longer audit trail but a larger history file.

config.history_max_age_days.effect: Drop configuration history entries older than this many days.
config.history_max_age_days.trade_off: A longer window keeps older changes visible but grows the history file.

config.history_max_bytes.effect: Keep the configuration history file under this many bytes; the oldest entries are dropped first.
config.history_max_bytes.trade_off: A larger bound keeps more history but costs more to read on every config edit.

chair.refusal_notice.effect: Send the bound chair a notice when a dispatch is refused before admission.
chair.refusal_notice.trade_off: Off keeps the inbox quiet; inbox makes refusals visible to the chair.

chair.auto_switch.effect: Allow the Claude UserPromptSubmit hook to checkpoint and switch accounts at the quota threshold.
chair.auto_switch.trade_off: Off keeps switching manual; on opens a new chair pane when an explicitly allowed account has headroom.

chair.switch_threshold.effect: Switch when either the five-hour or weekly cached Claude usage reaches this percentage.
chair.switch_threshold.trade_off: Lower switches sooner; higher leaves less headroom for the handoff.

chair.switch_accounts.effect: Ordered registered Claude account labels allowed as switch targets; empty allows none.
chair.switch_accounts.trade_off: An explicit list controls which signed-in accounts may receive the chair.

lanes.launch_retry_limit.effect: Number of transient graph launch retries before blocking the node.
lanes.launch_retry_limit.trade_off: More retries tolerate longer transient failures but delay a visible block.

lanes.launch_retry_first_seconds.effect: Initial delay in seconds before a graph launch retry; subsequent delays double.
lanes.launch_retry_first_seconds.trade_off: Shorter delays recover sooner but retry the host more often.

lanes.launch_retry_max_seconds.effect: Maximum graph launch retry delay, at least the first delay.
lanes.launch_retry_max_seconds.trade_off: A longer cap reduces repeated load but slows recovery.

lanes.silence_seconds.effect: Mark a provider observation silent after this many seconds without output or CPU progress; never kill it for silence.
lanes.silence_seconds.trade_off: Lower marks silence sooner; the process census and observation cadence stays unchanged.

lanes.context_handoff_tokens.effect: Context size, in tokens one provider call sent, at which the host stops a writer so the graph restarts it on a new route in the same worktree, from its handoff. The stop settles as a declared stop and follows the node's `on_stop` and the graph-wide `limits.continuations`; a node with no other route goes to the chair. Commits and uncommitted edits stay in place. 0 is off. Suggested setting 200000. Only providers that report each call's context (Claude) are stopped; others keep today's behaviour.
lanes.context_handoff_tokens.trade_off: Lower stops paying for very large contexts sooner but restarts more often, and a restart may lose working state that the handoff does not record; off until a trial shows restart does not lower completion.

lanes.token_budget.effect: Default fresh-token budget for writer lanes. 0 disables the budget. A run or template may set `attempt.token_budget`; project and host defaults come from domains.run.
lanes.token_budget.trade_off: Lower budgets limit spend sooner; higher budgets give writers more room to finish.

lanes.budget_action.effect: What a writer lane does after passing its fresh-token budget. wrap_up allows one continuation through the existing resume path; warn records the crossing and keeps the lane running; stop ends it immediately.
lanes.budget_action.trade_off: wrap_up gives the writer one clean chance to finish, warn prioritises completion, and stop prioritises a hard spend limit.

lanes.budget_grace.effect: Fraction of the token budget the host allows as grace before applying lanes.budget_action. 0.1 allows ten percent above the configured budget.
lanes.budget_grace.trade_off: A larger grace gives the writer more room to finish a clean step; zero applies the action at the configured threshold.

lanes.max_concurrency.effect: Default number of lanes one batch runs at once when any lane in it writes a worktree, resolved from the profile. An explicit dispatch concurrency wins.
lanes.max_concurrency.trade_off: Lower paces quota and memory and lengthens wall time; total tokens are unchanged.

lanes.max_concurrency_read_only.effect: Default number of lanes one batch runs at once when no lane in it writes a worktree, resolved from the profile. A lanes.max_concurrency you set yourself also caps it unless you set this knob too. An explicit dispatch concurrency wins.
lanes.max_concurrency_read_only.trade_off: Lower paces quota and memory and lengthens wall time; total tokens are unchanged. Read-only lanes start 2 s apart whatever this value.

lanes.local_cargo.effect: Which cargo subcommands a lane may run locally, enforced in the lane's cargo shim for every provider. all runs everything; check allows only `cargo check` (and subcommands that do not compile, such as fmt and metadata); none refuses every compiling command, `cargo check` included. A refused command exits non-zero with one line saying CI runs it. Set per run with --knob lanes.local_cargo=check, per graph node with `attempt.local_cargo`, or for the host under [knobs].
lanes.local_cargo.trade_off: check or none saves the build slot, CPU and about 1 GB of memory per rustc a lane would spend, and leaves tests and lints to CI; a lane cannot confirm its own change passes them before pushing. The shim is a cooperative control: a lane that runs rustc or ~/.cargo/bin/cargo directly bypasses it.

lanes.ci_scope.effect: What CI a writer lane runs or waits for, stated in its preamble and recorded with its value and source in the launch receipt and status. none: push the branch and report without dispatching, rerunning or waiting for CI; the chair runs CI once for the integrated batch. targeted: wait only for the checks that cover the change. full: wait for the full CI on the lane's pull request and fix what it reports. Set per run with --knob lanes.ci_scope=targeted, per graph node with `attempt.ci_scope` (`--set attempt.ci_scope=full`), or for the host under [knobs].
lanes.ci_scope.trade_off: Advisory guidance, not enforcement: it grants no CI dispatch authority and removes none. none saves runner minutes and the chair's waits; targeted or full lets a writer find its own CI failures before handoff at the cost of a CI run per lane.

lanes.gh_budget.effect: Advisory gh invocation budget per lane. The lane's gh wrapper counts each gh command; at the budget and each multiple of it the wrapper prints one warning and the command still runs. The count is recorded at settlement; the budget and its source appear in run --explain, the receipt and status. 0 turns the warning off; the count is still recorded.
lanes.gh_budget.trade_off: Never stops a lane and is not an API request cap: one paginated gh call is one invocation, and direct API clients or the real gh path bypass the count. Lower values warn sooner about quota-heavy polling.

lanes.isolation.effect: Whether an unpinned read-only graph node reads its bound checkout live (shared). A read-only lane pinned to a commit always gets an immutable source view, under every setting. Writers always keep one writer per worktree, so shared is refused on a writer node. Set per graph node with `attempt.isolation` or the `light` preset (`attempt.preset`),.
lanes.isolation.trade_off: shared starts faster but the lane sees edits made while it runs. Secret redaction and object integrity are unchanged.

lanes.supervision.effect: minimal marks a silent provider only after the longest silence interval (one hour) instead of lanes.silence_seconds. Set per graph node with `attempt.supervision` or the `light` preset.
lanes.supervision.trade_off: minimal reports a stalled lane later; deadlines, custody and confinement are unchanged.

lanes.receipts.effect: Delivery requested by a writer always runs and records its outcome. Set per graph node with `attempt.receipts` or the `light` preset.
lanes.receipts.trade_off: none suits read-only or scratch work; nothing is published or recorded as delivered.

lanes.prepare_deps.effect: Run pnpm install --frozen-lockfile on the host for a writer worktree with a pnpm lockfile and no completed install (node_modules/.modules.yaml), after head and route checks and before the provider starts.
lanes.prepare_deps.trade_off: false skips automatic dependency installation; the writer may then lack dependencies needed to work.

lanes.max_depth.effect: Maximum nested lane depth, including the first dispatched lane.
lanes.max_depth.trade_off: Lower limits delegation chains; higher permits deeper nested work.

lanes.publish.effect: Let every lane with open network, read-only lanes included, use the host's gh login, a git credential helper and gh to push their own branch and read or update issues and pull requests.
lanes.publish.trade_off: On (default) gives every networked lane your GitHub credential, so a malicious lane can extract the token and act outside the wrapper. false keeps publishing with the chair through host-side delivery.

lanes.sandbox.effect: Whether a macOS lane runs under the Seatbelt sandbox. The default auto runs every lane kind (including read-only) unsandboxed unless a configured route, narrowed network or parent floor requires sandboxing. Explicit off / --no-sandbox takes precedence over route, narrowed-network and parent floors where Provenant decides them, with a one-line warning naming the dropped restriction; an inherited operating-system sandbox is always reported honestly as effective. Off macOS every lane resolves as sandboxed, so Linux keeps refusing lanes. on / --sandbox explicitly opts into sandboxing. Set per run with --sandbox or --no-sandbox, per graph node or template with attempt.sandbox, or as the host default in [knobs]. The lane sees PROVENANT_SANDBOX=on or off, and status and the receipt show requested and effective mode and its source (parent, route, network, platform, knob or default).
lanes.sandbox.trade_off: Unsandboxed lanes work like the same CLI started by hand: they share host build caches and services, and can read on-disk credential stores and write outside their worktree. The environment is still rebuilt from an allowlist with hosted-cloud keys stripped, Git delivery stays host-owned with one writer per worktree, and host_policy path denials apply only to sandboxed lanes. A sandboxed lane reads domains.run.sandbox_cache_reads and never writes there.

balanced.description: Today's behaviour: every knob at its registry default.

economy.description: Lower lane concurrency, accepting slower runs.
